design_references.title: Test quality and architectural fitness steering
design_references.claim: The V&V rung ladder should compare native Go property testing with hegel-go before a cgo-backed beta dependency is adopted for swe-term's core.

hypothesis: hegel-go finds defect classes in swe-term's core that Go's native testing.F fuzzing does not, by enough margin to justify a cgo-backed beta dependency.
null_hypothesis: Native Go testing.F detects equivalent defect classes with equal or lower runtime/flakiness compared to hegel-go on a frozen defect corpus.
independent_variable: Property testing engine (native testing.F vs hegel-go).

variants.name: control
variants.description: Run the frozen core defect corpus with Go's standard testing.F fuzzing engine under the declared time budget.

variants.name: treatment
variants.description: Run the identical frozen core defect corpus with hegel-go under the same time and resource budget.

randomness.justification: Seeded pseudo-randomness across 3 equal-budget repetitions ensures coverage-guided fuzzing exploration is reproducible while enabling estimation of flaky-failure rate and runtime variability.

metrics.primary: distinct defect classes detected per equal-budget repetition
metrics.acceptance_rule: Compare engines on the same frozen defect corpus, seeds, task order, and time budget. Adoption is justified only if hegel-go detects materially more distinct defect classes with reproducible failures and acceptable runtime/flakiness; if native testing.F is equivalent or better, reject the adoption hypothesis.

evaluator.rubric: For each repetition, verify identical corpus, seed, timeout, CPU and memory limits, and environment allowlist; classify findings by defect class rather than raw failure count; replay every reported counterexample; distinguish a new class from a duplicate failure; record setup, runtime, flakiness, and minimization results separately; and treat build, native-library, or replay failures as invalid runs rather than missed defects.
